answer.summary: A roughly 200 ms network delay was injected into checkoutservice's outbound path. It affects calls to every dependency (and telemetry export), while downstream server execution remains fast, causing delays to accumulate into multi-second checkout latency.

answer.summary: The injected fault is packet loss affecting currencyservice. The service executes RPCs in sub-millisecond time, but callers intermittently wait seconds for successful responses in a retransmission/backoff pattern, propagating latency and open connections into frontend and checkoutservice.

evidence: emailservice_mem jumped after injection from a stable 40.2 MiB pre-fault to 202.6 MiB average post-fault, repeatedly reaching 256.0 MiB (425 samples near the ceiling).
The rise begins immediately after 1705600502000: memory grows from 42,196,992 bytes to 47,607,808 by 1705600509000 and then toward the 256 MiB ceiling.

Email RPC degradation is localized: checkoutservice SendOrderConfirmation rose from 4.3 ms average pre-fault to 474.3 ms post-fault (max 3397.8 ms); the emailservice server span rose from 0.3 ms to 30.6 ms (max 1521.2 ms).
emailservice CPU also rose from 0.31 to 18.56 average while memory was being stressed, consistent with active allocation/touching under memory pressure.
answer.summary: The injected fault is memory stress in emailservice. Its memory footprint abruptly expands from ~40 MiB and repeatedly hits a 256 MiB ceiling, while email RPC latency becomes severe and propagates into checkout PlaceOrder/SendOrderConfirmation.

evidence: emailservice_diskio was 0 immediately before injection (1705370094000) and surged to 661,153,800 at 1705370101000, then remained around 9.5–11.0 billion for the rest of the window.

At the same onset, emailservice CPU rose from about 0.30 to as high as 19.7 and memory jumped from 43,110,400 bytes to about 134 MB, consistent with heavy disk-write stress and page-cache/resource overhead.

No comparable step-change appeared in another service; emailservice SendOrderConfirmation remained successful, with 39 server spans averaging 1.3 ms and zero bad statuses, making downstream symptoms unlikely to be the root cause.
answer.summary: The injected fault is disk I/O stress in emailservice. Its disk activity changes abruptly from idle to sustained multi-billion-unit throughput just after the injection, accompanied by secondary CPU and memory pressure.

No frontend error increase or failed spans was observed; the impact is latency from currencyservice saturation.
answer.summary: The injected fault is CPU stress on currencyservice. Its container CPU rises sharply and repeatedly saturates near 50% at unchanged request load, producing cgroup-style scheduling stalls that propagate as higher checkout and frontend latency.

evidence: recommendationservice_mem was ~46,383,104 bytes through 1705533076000, then jumped to 205,955,072 at 1705533077000 and repeatedly reached 471,867,392 bytes (~450 MiB).
The post-injection 5-minute average recommendationservice memory rose from 46,367,280 bytes pre-injection to 280,743,147 bytes; no other service showed a comparable memory increase.
Memory-pressure side effects were localized there: recommendationservice CPU rose from 2.852 to 17.729 average and disk I/O from 0 to 34,214.611, while its socket count stayed fixed at 4.

Frontend spans to hipstershop.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations slowed from 8.5 ms average / 150.8 ms max to 383.5 ms average / 2532.5 ms max; recommendationservice server spans similarly rose from 4.1 ms to 88.1 ms average.
answer.summary: The injected fault is memory stress in recommendationservice. Its memory footprint abruptly surged immediately after injection and cycled at roughly 450 MiB, producing CPU/disk pressure and downstream recommendation latency while sockets remained normal.
